claims.title: Writer 0x005094C0 signature: thiscall copy-setter of a 3-DWORD record into SF local-translation fields with dirty flag
claims.statement: 0x005094C0 is thiscall: receiver in ECX (the SF-shaped object), exactly ONE 4-byte stack argument (RET 0x4) which is a POINTER to a contiguous 12-byte record. It performs: SF+34 <- [arg+0]; SF+38 <- [arg+4]; SF+3C <- [arg+8]; SF+28 <- 1 (byte dirty flag). No other writes. No return value (EAX clobbered by last load). No ID, parent, scale or rotation logic in the body.
claims.evidence: R1 extract rows 145735-145743 (extracts/R1_WRITER_005094C0.txt): 005094c0 MOV EAX,[ESP+4]; 005094c4 MOV EDX,[EAX]; 005094c6 MOV [ECX+0x34],EDX; 005094c9 MOV EDX,[EAX+4]; 005094cc MOV [ECX+0x38],EDX; 005094cf MOV EAX,[EAX+8]; 005094d2 MOV [ECX+0x3c],EAX; 005094d5 MOV byte [ECX+0x28],1; 005094d9 RET 0x4.
premises: thiscall convention assumed from ECX-receiver pattern + callee-cleaned single 4-byte arg (RET 0x4)
SF+34/+38/+3C semantics (local translation) is KNOWN CONTEXT supplied by parent, not re-derived here
byte +28 named 'dirty' per parent-provided writer designation, not proven semantic
claims.countermodel: If the writer were stdcall-with-pointer-return or took three scalar args, the [EAX] deref pattern would be absent and RET 0x4 would not match exactly one pushed DWORD; the observed deref at arg+0/+4/+8 rules out three separate scalar args.

claims.title: Callsite R2 @0x006A3727 (in 0x006A36F0): record = caller's own stack frame slot &F+0x3C with no in-body producer
claims.statement: Receiver = [caller+0x18]; record argument = LEA [ESP+0x40] = &F+0x3C (F = frame base after SUB ESP,0x4c), a 12-byte in-frame slot. No instruction in the admitted body stores to F+0x3C..F+0x47 before the call. Preceding out-parameter callees: 0x0085C280(this=[caller+4], out=&F+0xC) and 0x0085BFA0(this=[caller+4], out=&F+0x18); the record slot equals &F+0x18+0x24 (12-float buffer tail) or &F+0xC+0x30 (16-float buffer translation row) - either geometry fits exactly. After the writer: 0x0096CD10(this=&F+0x18, arg=&F+0={0,0,0}) then 0x00509510(this=[caller+0x18], arg=&F+0) writes rotation as CONSTANT ZEROS.
claims.evidence: R2 extract rows 607713-607747 with stack arithmetic: baseline ESP=F-4 after PUSH ESI; LEA [ESP+0x10]->F+0xC; LEA [ESP+0x1c]->F+0x18; LEA [ESP+0x40]->F+0x3C; zeros at F+0/F+4/F+8 via FLDZ/FST/FST/FSTP; 96CD10 this=&F+0x18 (LEA [ESP+0x20] at ESP=F-8); 509510 arg=&F+0.
premises: out-callees are assumed to consume their pushed args (RET n) since no in-body ADD ESP cleanup appears
extent of writes by 85C280/85BFA0 into their out-buffers is UNKNOWN (bodies not admitted)
claims.countermodel: If 85C280 and 85BFA0 both write fewer than 0x30 bytes, the record slot holds stale frame data from previous invocations (garbage-in) - a real static variant recorded as V2 in BARRIER_BACKLOG; it is not excluded within this package.

claims.title: Callsite R3 @0x0067B52E (in 0x0067B4F0): record = &F+0x3C; preceding getters 862850(arg1) and 85BFA0([caller+0]); rotation := constant zeros; ID-shaped [caller+0xC] flows AFTER the writer
claims.statement: Receiver = [caller+4]. Record = LEA [ESP+0x44] = &F+0x3C (same geometry as R2; baseline ESP=F-8 after PUSH ESI+PUSH EDI). Preceding out-callees: 0x00862850(this=arg1(stack arg 1, in EDI), out=&F+0xC) whose RETURN goes to 0x00509070(this=[caller+4], arg=ret); then 0x0085BFA0(this=[caller+0], out=&F+0x18). After the writer + zero-rotation (509510): second 862850(this=arg1, out=&F+0xC); its returned 3-float vector [ret+0/+4/+8] is length-computed (sqrt via 0x0095DA2E) => ||v||; then f32(||v|| * qword[0x00A7AF80]) and [caller+0xC] are passed to 0x004150F0, its result to 0x008B7210; finally tail CALL 0x006A34A0 with ECX=[caller+8] if nonzero.
claims.evidence: R3 extract rows 564107-564180; FPU chain decoded: FLD[ret+4]/FLD[ret]/FLD[ret+8], FLD ST1, FMULP ST2, FLD ST2, FMULP ST3, FXCH, FADDP ST2, FMUL ST0 (squares ST0=v8), FADDP => v0^2+v4^2+v8^2 stored, sqrt'd, reloaded, scaled by qword [0x00A7AF80], pushed with EAX=[ESI+0xC] to CALL 0x004150F0.
premises: 0x0095DA2E interpreted as CRT sqrt from the load/call/store pattern and its 0x0095xxxx CRT region address; body not read
qword at 0x00A7AF80 value NOT read (data address, not in code listing); known context contains a 0.01 factor in the position path but this package does not assert equality
[caller+0xC] described as numeric/ID-shaped only from its use as 004150F0 argument; semantics unknown
claims.countermodel: If [caller+0xC] were zero or a non-ID value, the ID-hint would be void - but the claim only asserts the FLOW (value passed after the writer), which is directly evidenced; the ID interpretation is explicitly UNVERIFIED and not part of the confirmed statement.

claims.title: Callsite R4 @0x0067C584 (in 0x0067C560): record = &F+0x3C; the ONLY preceding out-callee is 85BFA0([caller+0], out=&F+0x18) - discriminating witness for the record-producer hypothesis
claims.statement: Receiver = [caller+4]. Record = LEA [ESP+0x40] with baseline ESP=F-4 (only PUSH ESI) = &F+0x3C. Before the writer this body performs exactly one out-parameter call: 0x0085BFA0(this=[caller+0], out=&F+0x18). The record slot = &F+0x18+0x24 - the tail three floats of a 12-float buffer hypothesis. Rotation := constant zeros via 509510 after 96CD10(this=&F+0x18, &zeros). THEN (post-writer): if [caller+0xC] != 0: 862850(arg1, out=&F+0xC) -> 509070([caller+4], ret) -> 862850 again -> ||v|| -> 004150F0([caller+0xC], f32(||v||*q[0x00A7AF80])) -> 008B7210. post-writer calls cannot be the producer for THIS invocation (ordering), but stale-frame variant remains
claims.countermodel: If 85BFA0 writes < 0x30 bytes, R4's record = stale frame bytes; the consume-then-clear pattern (96CD10 on the same buffer with zeros AFTER the writer) would then be a coincidence of slot reuse. Neither direction proven inside this package.

claims.title: The position record does NOT distinguish resource ID / instance ID / parent / position / rotation - it is a bare 12-byte transform-shaped triple in all four callsites
claims.statement: In every admitted callsite the writer receives exactly a 12-byte triple. No ID, parent pointer, resource handle, rotation or scale field is present in or adjacent to the record. Rotation is written by a SEPARATE method (0x00509510) receiving a SEPARATE argument ({0,0,0} constants in R2/R3/R4; ret(85C0F0) in R5). ID-shaped values exist in the callers but never enter the record: [caller+0xC] (R3/R4 -> 004150F0 with scaled distance, AFTER the writer), arg2's field (R5 -> 43a550/72f580/72fce0 lookup, AFTER the writer), arg1 (R3/R4: 862850 receiver; R5: 85C0C0/85C0F0 receiver - the SOURCE OBJECT, identity unexamined).
claims.evidence: C2/C3/C4/C5 call sequences; R1 write-set; absence of any ID read in the writer path across all five extracts.
premises: 12 bytes cannot encode a NiNode parent pointer plus a triple without overlap; the writer consumes exactly [arg],[arg+4],[arg+8]
premise preserved: three float-shaped DWORDs != XYZ provenance - the triple is transform-SHAPED only
claims.countermodel: If one of the three DWORDs were an ID/flag rather than a float, the writer would still copy it identically - the writer cannot distinguish. This is exactly why XYZ provenance is NOT asserted; the claim is about the RECORD'S FIELD CONTENTS (no separate ID/parent channel), which is directly evidenced by the call ABI.

claims.title: Dominant record-producer hypothesis: 0x0085BFA0's out-buffer at &F+0x18 with the record at buffer offset +0x24 (translation-row geometry of a 12-float buffer)
claims.statement: R2/R3/R4 all call 85BFA0(this=<source object>, out=&F+0x18) immediately before the writer, and the record slot is exactly &F+0x18+0x24 in all three. R4 is the discriminating witness (only 85BFA0 precedes). The post-writer 0x0096CD10(this=&F+0x18, arg={0,0,0}) operating on the SAME buffer is consistent with a consume-then-clear/SetTranslation(0) pattern on a matrix-like stack object. In R2/R3 an alternate geometry also fits exactly: 85C280/862850(out=&F+0xC) writing a 16-float 4x4 would place its translation row at &F+0xC+0x30 = &F+0x3C.
claims.evidence: C2/C3/C4 sequences and slot arithmetic; consistency of the &F+0x18 buffer as 96CD10's this in R2/R3/R4.
premises: 85BFA0 extent >= 0x30 bytes REQUIRED for the hypothesis - NOT VERIFIED (body un-admitted)
row-major 12/16-float matrix layout is a structural hypothesis from slot geometry, not a read layout
claims.countermodel: Falsified if 85BFA0's body writes < 0x30 bytes at its out-param (then R4's record is stale/garbage), or if 85C280 (R2) / 862850 (R3) turn out to own the record via 4x4 extent while 85BFA0 writes only e.g. 0x24 bytes. Requires admission of 0x0085BFA0 (and secondarily 0x0085C280/0x00862850) to resolve.

claims.title: R2/R3/R4 are update/copy mechanisms, NOT historical data sources; R5 is a copy-initializer - the actual data source lies BEHIND the getters
claims.statement: R2/R3/R4 write rotation as constant {0,0,0} - no historical rotation restore shape; their position bytes come from in-frame buffers filled by getters. R5 creates a fresh receiver and copies BOTH position (85C0C0) and rotation (85C0F0) from source object arg1 - a spawn/duplicate shape. Per the preserved premise, none of these update/copy mechanisms is itself a recovered placement data source; the historical source, if any, is behind 85BFA0/85C0C0/85C0F0/862850's reads on their receivers ([caller+0], [caller+4], arg1).
claims.evidence: C2-C5 sequences; FLDZ-constant triples in R2/R3/R4; getter-fed rotation in R5.
premises: premise preserved: do not promote an update mechanism to a recovered data source
R5's 0x130-record construction after the position/rotation copy suggests instance-record creation, but its semantics are un-admitted
claims.countermodel: If 85BFA0/85C0C0 read directly from a world-message/descriptor (not from a scene node), R2/R3/R4/R5 could be intake paths of externally-provided transforms - that would CHANGE the classification from 'update mechanism' to 'intake'; not decidable in this window.

claims.statement: No instruction in the five admitted subregions writes SF+30 (the known NiNode-family link) or any parent field of the receiver. No NiNode attach/detach call is identified. The candidate link-setter is 0x00509070 (called as this=SF-receiver with a getter-returned pointer in R2/R3/R4) - body un-admitted, semantics unknown. R5's 0x00509190(receiver, 0) and R3/R4's tail 0x006A34A0(this=[caller+8]) are additional unqualified candidates. Therefore the written node's qualification as instance root vs internal NIF node CANNOT be established from this package.

premises: absence-of-write in the window does NOT mean absence in the program - only that this package cannot qualify the node role
known context SF+30->NiNode-family is parent-supplied; 509070-as-SF+30-setter is a hypothesis, not asserted
claims.countermodel: If 509070's body writes SF+30 := arg, the fed node identity becomes resolvable next package; if it writes something else (e.g., SF+04 or a list append), the node-role question stays open. Either way this claim's negative stands for THIS window.
